# test-floors.txt — one floor per integration target, checked by
# scripts/test-floor.sh against the whole-suite tier log:
#
#   bash scripts/test-floor.sh --targets .github/test-floors.txt --log tmp/logs/suite.log
#
# A FLOOR, BECAUSE THE FAILURE MODE HERE IS AN ABSENCE. `cargo test`
# exits 0 on "0 passed; 0 failed", so a target that selected nothing
# looks exactly like a target that passed everything. A suite emptied
# from the inside — every test renamed, feature-gated out, or moved to
# another file — reports green having stopped checking that this driver
# reads Btrfs. A target missing from the log counts as zero, so a suite
# that stopped being BUILT fails here too.
#
# WHERE THESE NUMBERS LIVED BEFORE. In .github/workflows/ci.yml, one per
# `cargo test --test <name>` step, across a job of fifty-odd steps. That
# arrangement had the guard and the hazard in one place: a suite absent
# from the list executed nowhere at all, and two of them were (#70). The
# tiers are derived from the tests now, so the workflow no longer names
# suites — and the floors moved here rather than being lost, which is
# the point of this file.
#
# THE NUMBERS ARE MEASURED, not guessed: each is what that target
# executed on a known-good run of `chore test` (the whole suite, release
# profile). They move UP with the suite and never down: raising one when
# tests are added is bookkeeping, lowering one is a decision someone has
# to write down in a diff.
#
# `lib` is the library's own unit tests, which `cargo test` reports as
# `Running unittests src/lib.rs`.
#
# <target> <floor>
